We need to return all possible precursors of applying the template (from previous step) to the molecule. We have template_id 1914384 and mapped_rxn given. The initial molecule is the product? The mapped_rxn shows forward reaction: left side is reactants? Actually mapped_rxn: '([CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18])>>([CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18])'

So forward reaction: reactant (left) -> product (right). The product is the initial molecule? The initial_molecule given: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

But note mapping: In product side, there is [CH3:1][C@H:2]... but initial molecule has [CH2:1]=[C:2]... So maybe the initial molecule is the reactant side? Let's compare: left side of mapped_rxn: ([CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1... )=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]) . This includes a double bond between C2 and CH9? Actually /[C:2]... = [CH:9]/... So left side is an alkene with CH3 attached to C2? The product side: [CH3:1][C@H:2]... [C@@H:9]1... [C@@:13]1([OH:14])... So product is saturated (single bonds) with OH at C13.

Our initial molecule: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]... ) [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])... This matches left side but with CH2 at atom1 not CH3, and double bond between C1 and C2? Actually left side has [CH3:1]/[C:2]... = [CH:9]/... So CH3 attached to C2, double bond to CH9. Our initial has [CH2:1]=[C:2]... and then [C@@H:9]... So seems similar but CH2 vs CH3 and double bond orientation maybe same.

Thus the initial molecule is the reactant side of the template (the one to be transformed). Applying the retrosynthetic template should give precursors: the product side? Wait retrosynthetic template is reverse of forward reaction. So applying template to product yields reactants. But we have initial molecule as product? Actually we want precursors of applying the template as result of template_search. The template_search gave a template that presumably can be applied to the target molecule (initial_molecule) to generate precursors. So we need to apply the template (retro) to the initial molecule. The tool apply_template expects target SMILES and template_id. So we should call apply_template with molecule_smiles = initial_molecule (but need proper SMILES without atom mapping). The initial_molecule includes atom mapping numbers. We need a valid SMILES without mapping. The mapping is [CH2:1]=[C:2]... etc. We need to strip mapping. Could we just use the SMILES without mapping? Probably we need to provide a SMILES string; the tool may accept mapping? Likely not. We need to convert to standard SMILES. The core structure: CH2=C(c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C(=O)C(F)(F)F)C1O? Wait let's decode: [CH2]=[C]([c]1[cH]... ) [C@@H]1[CH2][CH2][CH2][C@@]1([OH]) [C]([F])([F])[F]. So product is a cyclobutane? Actually ring of 4 carbons? It's a cyclobutane? The pattern: C@@H:9 1 CH2:10 CH2:11 CH2:12 C@@:13 1(OH) ... So a cyclobutane? Actually numbering: C9 is attached to ring start, then CH2 10,11,12, then C13 closes ring. So a cyclobutane with OH at C13 and attached carbonyl CF3? Wait C13 has OH and also attached to C15 with three Fs? Actually C13 is carbon bearing OH and attached to C15? The SMILES: [C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18] So C13 attached to OH and to C15 which is CF3. So it's a cyclobutane with a side chain CF3 carbonyl? Actually C15 is attached to C13, and has three Fs, no carbonyl. So it's a CF3 group attached to C13.

Thus the retrosynthetic step likely is a hydroboration? Actually forward reaction: alkene + something yields saturated alcohol? The forward reaction shows left side: CH3 attached to C2, double bond to CH9, and C13 carbonyl (C=O). Right side: saturated with OH at C13. So transformation is reduction of alkene to alkane and reduction of carbonyl to alcohol? Actually left side has C13(=O) (carbonyl) and right side has C13(OH). So it's a hydrogenation of alkene and reduction of carbonyl? Might be a catalytic hydrogenation? But anyway.

Applying retro template to product (our initial) would give precursors: the left side (alkene + carbonyl). So we need to output list of precursors: two molecules? The left side appears as a single molecule? Actually left side is a single molecule with both alkene and carbonyl. So the retro step yields one precursor? But the template may split into two? The forward reaction shows one reactant -> one product. So retro yields one precursor (the same as left side). However the required format expects list of lists of SMILES of each precursor. So we would output something like [['CH3...']]? But need correct SMILES.

We need to apply template using tool apply_template to get precursors. Let's call apply_template with molecule_smiles = the product SMILES (without mapping). We need to construct SMILES. Let's approximate: The product SMILES: CH3 attached to C2? Wait product side has CH3 at atom1 attached to C2 which is chiral, aromatic ring, etc. But our initial is left side? I'm confused.

Better: Use apply_template with the given initial_molecule (with mapping) maybe tool can handle mapping? Not sure. Let's try call apply_template with the SMILES stripped of mapping: we need to generate a SMILES string. Could approximate: "C=C(c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C(=O)C(F)(F)F)C1O"? Wait left side has carbonyl C13(=O) attached to CF3? Actually left side: [C:13](=[O:14]) and [C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18] attached to C13? The SMILES: ...[CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18] So carbonyl carbon attached to CF3 carbon? That's an acyl CF3? So it's a trifluoroacetyl group? Actually C13 is carbonyl carbon, attached to CF3 carbon (C15). So it's a trifluoroacetyl group attached to cyclobutane.

Thus left side SMILES: "C=C(c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C(=O)C(F)(F)F)C1" plus maybe CH3? Wait left side also has CH3 attached to C2? The left side has [CH3:1]/[C:2]... So CH3 attached to C2. So overall left side SMILES: "CC(=C(c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C(=O)C(F)(F)F)C1)"? Actually CH3 attached to C2 which is double bonded to CH9. So CH3- C2 = CH9 - rest. So CH3-CH=... So maybe "CC(=C(c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C(=O)C(F)(F)F)C1)"? That seems plausible.

Thus the precursor is that molecule. So output list of one list containing that SMILES.

But to be safe, we can call apply_template to get actual result. Let's attempt.
